observations: Four correct simplified pictograms and protective/disposal examples, scoped by explicit alt-text warning that these are not full substance information. Main symbols/action recognizable at 360 and 680; tiny secondary statements are not independent reading evidence.

At the positive Cu cathode the microscopic upward arrow leads from the Cu representation toward two 2e− tokens, visually showing electron release at a reduction electrode. Incoming wire electrons should be consumed in Cu2+ reduction, not emitted upward.
The salt bridge has an upper leftward arrow immediately adjacent to the right-hand K+ label as well as a lower rightward arrow; K+ movement toward the Cu half-cell is not unambiguously encoded.

Only a voltmeter is shown in the outer circuit while steady electron-flow arrows are drawn. A voltage measurement alone does not establish a load-carrying sustained current. Retain valid colours/halfcells/equations; correct these specific directional/circuit representations before current V acceptance.

Named formulas and main acid/base effects are correct as Arrhenius symbolic shorthand. H+(aq) is solvated-proton shorthand, not a naked proton; independently reviewed cases explicitly make that limit clear. Cartoon particle cloud is overview, not a quantified solution composition. Main motifs/formulas recognizable at 360, all label details readable at 680.

In the central protolysis example the molecule labelled H3O+ is drawn as an O sphere with two visible white H spheres, matching the neighbouring two-H water shape. No third H or explicit occlusion cue is present. The point of this goal is the added proton, so the drawing must visibly represent three H attached to O or use an unambiguous formula-only species.

The basic-mixture panel additionally repeats two-H water-like shapes on purple species amidst Na+ labels and combines blue/red OH− shapes. Exact particle identities are not clear enough to grant current scientific V approval. Correct explicit species shapes while keeping the valid conjugate-pair and mixture overview.
